comment: THE ONE SOURCE of the Cache-Control of plane-backed pages (contract 12.7.6). next.config.js headers() and tests/headers-allowlist.test.ts both read this file. A plane-backed page is force-dynamic; the CDN keeps its HTML for 5 minutes and may serve it stale for 10 more while it refreshes: worst case 5 (pointer CDN) + 5 + 10 minutes behind a publish. Route handlers and image responses set the same value themselves (publicDataHeaders in headers.ts): Next adds its own Cache-Control to metadata routes, so next.config.js headers() would double it (measured on sitemap.xml). Everything per-user or per-tier, and every /api route, is private, no-store.

thinNoindex.comment: A THIN card page (listed but below INDEX_FLOOR_CENTS) is still a dynamic render: noindex does not stop crawling, so it is cached a day at the CDN and carries X-Robots-Tag (set by the page via thinHeaders in headers.ts, not by a config glob, because only the render knows the mask)

cdnComment: THE CDN COPY THAT ACTUALLY APPLIES (2026-10-16, DECISIONS.md "The CDN finally caches the public pages"). On Vercel a force-dynamic page's own Cache-Control (private, no-store) replaces the Cache-Control above, so no page was ever CDN-cached. Vercel-CDN-Cache-Control is read by Vercel's CDN first, from a function or from next.config.js, and never reaches the browser. It goes ONLY on pagesCdn: public pages whose server render reads no market (getCountry), cookie, header or session, so one copy is right for every visitor (tests/headers-allowlist.test.ts walks each page's imports to prove it). A day fresh and a day of stale-while-revalidate (owner, 2026-10-17: twelve hours at the least): the plane publishes once a day, and a release empties the CDN. The pages that read the visitor's market are pagesCdnMarket, below.
cdnMarketComment: ONE CDN COPY PER PAGE PER MARKET (2026-10-17, DECISIONS.md "Crawlers get the US copy from the CDN" and "Every market gets its own CDN copy"). These pages render in the visitor's market (getCountry: the country cookie when it names a market, else Vercel's IP country through normalizeCountry, else the US), and Vercel's CDN keys on neither a cookie nor geo, so next.config.js turns the market into the cache key. A US render keeps the bare URL. A request that certainly renders another market is rewritten to ?_mk=<its cookie> (AU, UK, SG, CA, EU) or, with no cookie, ?_mk=<its IP country> (marketGeo: the codes normalizeCountry sends to a market other than the US), and is cached there. Anything else (a cookie naming no market, no cookie and a country the rules do not list) is rewritten to ?_mk=1, never stored. Vercel-CDN-Cache-Control goes only on a request whose key holds its own market's render, and never on one that arrived carrying _mk. Static has/missing rules: no middleware. No ISR: an ISR write is billed per 8 KB and costs several renders, and a long-tail page a crawler reads once a day would pay it every day. tests/headers-allowlist.test.ts evaluates the rules against getCountry for every cookie and every two-letter country code.
